record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: If u is a palindromic fixed point of a primitive morphism, must there exist a class P₀ morphism whose fixed point has the same language as u?

evidence.quote: (Class P conjecture, due to A. Hof, O. Knill and B. Simon, [34]): Let u be a ﬁxed point of a primitive morphism. If u has infinitely many palindromic factors (u is palindromic, for short), then a morphism of class P₀ exists, whose ﬁxed point has the same language as the word u.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let A be a finite alphabet and A* the free monoid of finite words over A. A morphism φ: A* → A* is called primitive if there exists an integer n ≥ 1 such that, for every pair of letters a, b ∈ A, the letter b occurs in φ^n(a). An infinite word u ∈ A^ℕ is a fixed point of φ if φ(u) = u. The language L(u) of u is the set of all finite factors (contiguous subwords) of u. A finite word w is a palindrome if it equals its reverse. The infinite word u is called palindromic if L(u) contains infinitely many palindromes.

A morphism φ: A* → A* is said to belong to class P₀ if there exist a palindrome p ∈ A* and palindromes q_a ∈ A* (one for each a ∈ A) such that φ(a) = p q_a for every a ∈ A.

Question: Suppose u is a palindromic infinite word that is a fixed point of some primitive morphism. Must there exist a morphism ψ of class P₀ admitting a fixed point v with L(v) = L(u)?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (due to Hof, Knill and Simon) is resolved in the negative: a ternary counterexample to the class-P question was provided by Labbé (2014, Electronic J. Combinatorics; arXiv:1307.1589). The binary case was confirmed earlier (B. Tan, 2007). Subsequent work (Labbé–Pelantová, 2015) shows that, up to conjugacy, primitive palindromic substitutive subshifts are generated by morphisms close to but not always exactly of class P, so the original question has a negative answer in general.

status_evidence.title: A Counterexample to a Question of Hof, Knill and Simon
status_evidence.snippet: Counterexample provided to the class P question of Hof, Knill and Simon.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is false in general: an explicit counterexample exists.

status_evidence.title: On a question of Hof, Knill and Simon on palindromic substitutive systems
status_evidence.snippet: Every rich primitive substitutive subshift is generated by at most two morphisms each of which is conjugate to a morphism of class P.
status_evidence.claim: Partial positive results hold up to conjugacy, but the literal class P₀ statement fails.
